Hi Sofia,

Thanks for sending over Helion's redlines. We reviewed the insurance section in the attached MSA redlines and want to propose a short path to get to execution without blocking your procurement cycle. High level: we need confirmation of coverage minimums, an Additional Insured endorsement that matches our naming, and either an insurer endorsement or COI plus endorsement stub (COI alone won't be sufficient for legal in most cases).

Proposed next steps (simple MAP):
- By Mon 3/5: Helion to confirm insurer name and NAIC, and confirm whether endorsement or policy wording will be provided.
- By Thu 3/8: Broker to deliver COI + endorsement PDF (or insurer letter) that shows the exact additional insured language and waiver of subrogation if applicable.
- By Fri 3/10: Redwood legal to confirm acceptance or request a narrow fix.

Coverage asks we've surfaced to Legal (see attachments):
- Commercial General Liability: $2,000,000 per occurrence / $4,000,000 aggregate
- Professional Liability / E&O: $2,000,000 per claim / aggregate
- Cyber Liability: $2,000,000 aggregate (if Helion will be processing Redwood customer data)
- Automobile Liability: $1,000,000 combined single limit (where relevant)
- Workers' Compensation: statutory limits

Endorsement items: Additional Insured for "Redwood Inference, Inc., its subsidiaries and affiliates" (exact naming in attachment), primary and non-contributory wording, waiver of subrogation to the extent permitted by law. We typically accept standard ISO Additional Insured forms (CG 20 10/CG 20 37 or equivalent) but can accept insurer-specific endorsement language as long as it matches the effect of those forms.

I've attached our redline PDF and a short COI template to help your broker. If Helion prefers, we can accept a certificate with an attached executed endorsement from the insurer rather than a policy excerpt.

If it's helpful, I'll loop in Aditya (legal) for the final wording.

Thanks — let me know if the MAP dates look OK and I'll mark up any specific language Legal wants to see.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Hi all — James from ACME Brokerage here.

Quick note on carrier-side practicality: we can issue an Additional Insured endorsement and COI that follow ISO equivalents, but two points to confirm with Redwood Legal before we issue:
- Exact naming. We can do a blanket Additional Insured for "Redwood Inference, Inc., its subsidiaries and affiliates"; if Redwood needs specific DBA or parent entity names listed we can add them.
- Policy form preference. Most carriers will use CG 20 10/CG 20 37 style language; if Redwood needs a CG 20 26 (completed operations) or other specific variant, flag that.
- Effective date / retroactive date: for ongoing services, some carriers want a specific effective date for endorsement issuance; please confirm whether Helion providing the endorsement at time of signature is OK, or whether you need retroactive coverage to the start of the services.

Also: Helion's cyber tower is short of the $2M threshold. We can submit a short-term increase request, but carrier approval may take 5–7 business days.

I'll prepare a COI + draft endorsement PDF and target sending it by Tue 3/6, pending the naming confirmation and cyber update.

Hi all — looping in from Redwood Legal with specifics so your team has an actionable checklist.

Short answers to James' questions:
1) Naming: "Redwood Inference, Inc., its subsidiaries and affiliates" is acceptable. Please ensure the endorsement language mirrors that naming exactly. If the carrier will only do a parent-level name, add the full legal entity and include "and its affiliates."
2) Form: We accept CG 20 10 / CG 20 37 forms or insurer-specific language that provides materially equivalent coverage (i.e., Additional Insured status for ongoing operations and completed operations where CG 20 37 applies). If the carrier proposes CG 20 26 only, flag that — CG 20 26 is limited to completed ops and not sufficient alone for ongoing services.
3) Waiver of subrogation: acceptable where allowed by law — insurer endorsement or policy language should show waiver in favor of Redwood.
4) Primary/non-contributory: insurer must endorse to confirm primary and non-contributory treatment to the extent permitted by law.
5) COI vs endorsement: a COI without an attached, insurer-executed endorsement is not sufficient. We will accept a certificate if the executed endorsement PDF is attached or if the insurer issues a letter on carrier letterhead confirming the Additional Insured status and waiver clauses.

Deadlines: we can accept a COI + executed endorsement PDF by 2028-03-10 to keep the timeline. If Helion needs more time to increase cyber limits, please let us know and we'll discuss interim mitigations (e.g., contractual risk allocation for the initial 30 days).

Please send the COI + endorsement to gs-contracts@redwood.ai and loop me on any carrier communications if you need technical escalation.

Thanks — Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
